title: Strings: bytes, terminators, and safe views
goal: Distinguish bytes, the terminator and a non-owning slice, and state the units of a text report.

prerequisites.text: Modules 1–2: expressions, comparisons, types, references, and checked cin.
Follow the prerequisite links: cpp.two-dimensional-arrays. New constructs are introduced before the assignment.

sections.title: Character arrays and C strings
paragraphs: The three letters in cat occupy four array cells with the terminator. This storage size is not automatically the word’s length.

char word[4]{'c','a','t','\0'} is a C string with three letters and a null terminator. char letters[3]{'c','a','t'} is a three-char array, but not a C string. Passing it to a function that searches for \0 violates that function’s precondition.

The array size includes terminator storage; the text length before it does not. An embedded zero byte ends a C string before the buffer ends. Demonstrate the distinction with bounded valid examples, never by executing an unterminated read.

sections.title: std::string owns a sequence
paragraphs: std::string tracks its own char count and may contain embedded \0 data. size() counts chars, not visible letters. c_str() supplies a null-terminated compatibility buffer; do not retain its pointer across string mutation or owner destruction.

operator>> reads a whitespace-delimited token. getline reads a line without its terminating newline and retains internal spaces. Choose according to the format: a project name may contain spaces while a command code may be one ASCII token.
In the three-byte string a, 0, b, zero is inside the data. std::string stores its length separately and does not stop traversal at that byte.

sections.title: Length and terminator
paragraphs: Predict the array size, string length and numerical value of the middle byte.

reveal.title: Reveal output and trace execution
paragraphs: The first two numbers refer to different types: array size and string length. The third shows a null byte inside the string.

tables.caption: Trace for this run
rows: Three letters plus the null terminator.

sections.title: ASCII and UTF-8
paragraphs: In UTF-8 one code point can occupy several bytes. Four Cyrillic letters commonly occupy eight bytes, while a perceived character may itself contain several code points. size() promises neither code-point nor grapheme count.

The lab classifies only ASCII A…Z, a…z, 0…9, and ordinary space. Other bytes count as other without modifying the original string. This is an explicit limited contract, not Unicode normalization or collation.
In UTF-8, é occupies two bytes. An ASCII classifier counts both bytes as other; it makes no claim about the number of letters on screen.

sections.title: string_view does not own
paragraphs: std::string_view from <string_view> holds a pointer and a length into another object’s text. It is convenient for read-only parameters but does not extend a std::string’s lifetime. A view’s substr creates another view; converting to std::string creates an owned copy.

A view need not end in \0. Do not pass view.data() to a C-string API without proving termination. Never return a view into a local string or mutate an owner in a way that may relocate its buffer while the view is in use.
In key=value, the right-hand view refers to the characters after '='. While the owner is alive and its storage is unchanged, reading does not require a copy.

sections.title: A view with a live owner
paragraphs: Locate '=' in key=value. Trace the positions that form the two slices.

sections.title: Search, emptiness, and byte classes
paragraphs: find returns a position or std::string::npos. Check the result and bounds before substr because the current runtime does not support exceptions. An empty line may be valid under the format; it differs from a failed getline with no line available.

For <cctype>, pass a value representable as unsigned char or EOF; a negative char is invalid. Direct unsigned-char comparisons against ASCII boundaries avoid locale-dependent classification here. An individual UTF-8 byte must not be edited as though it were a whole letter.
A missing '=' gives npos. Check it before adding 1 or taking the right-hand slice.

sections.title: Text-interface tests
paragraphs: Test an empty line, spaces only, mixed letters and digits, internal spaces, and UTF-8. The lab limit is 200 bytes. Input must contain exactly one line; a second line, even empty, is extra data.

Preserve the original bytes and expected categories without claiming to count human-perceived characters. Next, a struct will group text, numbers, and status into one record without mixing their meanings.
One empty line differs from no line. In the first case getline obtains a record of length 0; in the second no record is extracted.

sections.title: Now try your own task
paragraphs: Build an ASCII report in which each byte belongs to exactly one of four classes. Length is measured in bytes.
Label A, b, space, 1, 2 and !. Predict separately what happens with é.

selfcheck.prompt: What does the program print for the cat array and the string a, 0, b?
feedback: Yes. The terminator is part of the array, and the string holds all three bytes.
sizeof includes the terminator, and the string is not truncated by the internal zero.
The byte value is printed, not its index.

selfcheck.prompt: What does size() count in a UTF-8 std::string?
options: char elements, meaning bytes on the 8-bit-char target
selfcheck.feedback: Code points and graphemes require a separate algorithm.
A view has a length, not a termination guarantee.

selfcheck.prompt: Are an empty line and no line equivalent?
selfcheck.feedback: An empty line can be read successfully.

selfcheck.prompt: What does npos after find mean?
selfcheck.feedback: Check the result before calculating a substring.

selfcheck.prompt: What is needed to accept this lab?
options: Source, actual results, original tests, and a contract explanation
selfcheck.feedback: A progress flag is not evidence of independent mastery.

selfcheck.prompt: Why does é contribute two other bytes under this contract? What would change in the tests if Unicode letters had to be counted?
selfcheck.feedback: A blank line is represented by a newline. Do not treat UTF-8 byte length as a letter count.

practice.title: One-line byte report
practice.task: Read one line of at most 200 bytes. Print bytes letters digits spaces other using ASCII classes; an empty line is valid, but no line or a second line is invalid.

cases.label: Letters, digits, a space and a sign

criteria: The sum of letters, digits, spaces and other must equal bytes. Compare a blank line with absent input and test UTF-8.
Byte length and perceived-text length are different contracts.
Do not retain string_view into a temporary string. Do not call isalpha with a potentially negative char.
Add two cases of your own, including a rejection if the interface allows one. Explain one boundary result.
Keep the source, exact input and observed output.
practice.hint: A blank line is represented by a newline. Do not treat UTF-8 byte length as a letter count.

steps.action: Label A, b, space, 1, 2 and !. Predict separately what happens with é.
steps.why: Each byte is classified, so the four counts must sum to the length.
steps.expected: Ab 12! contains 2 letters, 2 digits, 1 space and 1 other byte.

steps.action: Allow an empty line and reject no record, an overlong line or a second line. Compare bytes against ASCII ranges.
steps.why: getline distinguishes a zero-length record from no record.

steps.action: The sum of letters, digits, spaces and other must equal bytes. Compare a blank line with absent input and test UTF-8.
steps.why: A multibyte character tests the report’s unit of measurement.
steps.expected: A blank line gives five zeroes. An absent line is rejected, and é gives 2 other bytes.

terms.definition: the zero char marking the end of a C string.
a non-owning char sequence with a length.
encoding code points using variable-length byte sequences.
a numeric position in the Unicode code space.
a perceived text unit, sometimes containing multiple code points.
a special no-position value returned by search.
